title: Your service
tomorrow: one trait to work on. how does Amira pick just one?

segments.voice: Yesterday, my study: one book, and then the next. Knowledge is meant to turn into something you do with your hands.

A church basement on a Saturday morning: folding tables, canned beans, a line out the door, volunteers who know each other by first name. On the wall, painted by someone long ago, is a line from the Gospel of Matthew. A Muslim volunteer reads it and stops, because it sounds familiar. A hadith says something remarkably close. So what is it about serving people that two traditions put almost the same words to?
screen: `A SATURDAY PANTRY LINE.` → `A VERSE ON THE WALL.` → `IT SOUNDS FAMILIAR.`

segments.voice: Here's the wall, in the King James words. Jesus tells of a king who says to the people at his right: "I was sick, and ye visited me." They ask when. He answers: "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me." Now the hadith, in Sahih Muslim. It's a hadith qudsi, in which the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reports God's own words. On the Day of Resurrection, God says: son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. The person asks: how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? God answers: didn't you know My servant was sick, and you didn't visit him? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him. The same follows for food, and for water. That's what's shared: two traditions saying that care for the sick and the hungry never stops at the person in front of you. It reaches God. And one honest difference. Christians hear, in Matthew, Jesus the king saying the deed was done to him. In the hadith, God doesn't become the sick person; He is found with him, near the one who needs care. Each reads its own words its own way, and neither needs the other to be wrong. Your service is a regular place to go and find that.
screen: `I WAS SICK, AND YE VISITED ME.` · `YOU WOULD HAVE FOUND ME WITH HIM.` · `SHARED: IT REACHES GOD.` · `DIFFERENT: HOW GOD IS THERE.` · then, large: `MY SERVICE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person who is sick, hungry, or alone this week: someone you know, or a face from a line somewhere. Stay with them for the sit. Before you open your eyes, choose one regular way you could show up: a day, a place, a person.

segments.voice: Your service: a regular way you show up for others. In the hadith, God is found with the sick.

notes: Unity thread (wisdom day): shared, each in its own words and source: Matthew 25:36 and 25:40 (KJV) and the hadith qudsi in Sahih Muslim 2569 (sick, food, water; 'you would have found Me with him'). Honest difference: Christians read Matthew as Jesus the king identifying with the least; in the hadith God is found with the sick, not identified with him. No ranking; 'neither needs the other to be wrong'. A Christian reviewer should confirm the Matthew framing.
Muslim 2569: paraphrased; confirm numbering and wording ('Lord of the worlds'; the same for food and water).
The fork reveal's 'My servant' and 'the pantry on the wall' do not claim the hadith covers non-Muslims explicitly; a Keeper may want to confirm the inclusive reading.
